# Reading an Indemnity Clause

The three questions that matter: who indemnifies whom, for which claims,
and with what cap. A mutual indemnity that covers "any breach of this
agreement" with no cap is the widest possible exposure and is worth a
negotiation round on its own.

Look for the defense obligation separately from the indemnity itself.
"Defend and indemnify" means the other side pays your lawyers from day one;
indemnify alone means you front the costs and argue about them after
judgment. The difference in cash-flow terms can exceed the damages.

Carve-outs decide the real risk. Standard practice excludes claims arising
from the indemnified party's own negligence, and caps everything except
confidentiality breaches and IP infringement at twelve months of fees paid.
